key_insight: The PEA organic spacer improves crystal morphology and suppresses lattice defects, slowing degradation relative to BA in two-dimensional lead iodide perovskites under ambient light and thermal stress.
engineering_relevance: Spacer selection can improve perovskite durability, but long-term device stability also requires structural and chemical engineering, surface passivation, and encapsulation.
method: Compared BA2PbI4 and PEA2PbI4 perovskites with different organic spacers.
Assessed ambient photo- and thermal stability using confocal micro-Raman spectroscopy.
Used X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy to investigate chemical degradation.
evidence_signal: Freshly exfoliated nanoflakes showed comparable room-temperature luminescence, while PEA-based crystals degraded more slowly despite both materials losing organic components and decomposing into PbI2 and metallic Pb.
watch_item: Improved material stability does not establish long-term device durability; the stability–performance trade-off remains unresolved.
paper_title: Impact of organic spacer cations on the light and thermal stability of two-dimensional lead halide perovskites
